================================================================================
MASTER REPORT TEMPLATE — Comprehensive Personal Astrology Analysis
Company Use Only | Generated from: Birth Date + Birth Time + Birth Location
================================================================================

HOW TO USE THIS TEMPLATE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Every report is generated from three client inputs:
  1. {{BIRTH_DATE}}      (e.g., March 14, 1992)
  2. {{BIRTH_TIME}}      (exact time strongly encouraged — required for Rising sign and houses)
  3. {{BIRTH_LOCATION}}  (city, state/province, country)

From these, the engine computes:
  - The natal chart (planets in signs, degrees, and houses; Ascendant; aspects)
  - The element/modality balance of the natal chart
  - The synastry blueprint (what the client's own chart says about their relational needs)
  - The transit overlay for {{REPORT_DATE}} → {{REPORT_DATE + 1 YEAR}} (today's sky on the natal chart)

Placeholder key: {{DOUBLE_BRACES}} are auto-filled from the chart calculation.
Bracketed [ITALIC NOTES] are instructions to the report writer/generator and are
removed from the final client-facing document.

Report length target: 25–40 pages. Tone: warm, insightful, specific. Never
generic sun-sign-horoscope copy — every sentence should trace back to the
client's actual placements.

REPORT STRUCTURE AT A GLANCE
  Part I    — Introduction: The "Top Three" (Sun, Moon, Rising)
  Part II   — Birth Chart: Personality Overview
              A. Planetary placements and meanings
              B. Planets in the twelve houses
              C. Major aspects
              D. SECTION CLOSER: The Four Elements in your chart (excess & lack)
  Part III  — Synastry Report: What to Look For in a Partner AND in Friends
              (equal weight given to both)
  Part IV   — Transit Report: Weekly Predictions for the Next 12 Months
  Part V    — Closing Integration & Disclaimer

================================================================================
PART I — INTRODUCTION: THE "TOP THREE" (SUN, MOON, RISING)
================================================================================

[This section always comes first. It explains WHY the top three matter before
any interpretation is given, then interprets the client's own top three.]

1.1  WHY THE TOP THREE ARE THE FOUNDATION OF EVERY READING
  - Most people "know" only their Sun sign — the tip of the iceberg. A real
    chart reading begins with the three placements that carry the most weight:
  - The SUN ({{SUN_SIGN}}): your core identity, ego, vitality, and life
    purpose. The sign you were "born under." It answers: Who am I becoming?
    The Sun is the engine of the chart — the conscious will and the hero's
    journey of the lifetime.
  - The MOON ({{MOON_SIGN}}): your emotional nature, instincts, subconscious
    patterns, and what makes you feel safe. It answers: What do I need? The
    Moon governs private self, memory, mood, and how you nurture and wish to be
    nurtured.
  - The RISING SIGN / ASCENDANT ({{ASCENDANT_SIGN}}): the mask you wear, first
    impressions, physical presence, and the lens through which you approach
    life. It answers: How does the world meet me? The Rising also sets the
    house system, so it shapes how every other planet expresses itself.
  - WHY THEY WORK AS A TRIAD: The Rising is the cover of the book, the Sun is
    the story, and the Moon is what the story secretly means to the author.
    Read together, they explain the recurring tension most clients recognize
    instantly — "why people see me differently than I feel inside."
  - [Writer note: cite the client's exact degrees and, where relevant, note a
    "cusp" situation (e.g., born within ~2° of a sign change) and why the birth
    time resolves it.]

1.2  YOUR TOP THREE, INTERPRETED
  - {{SUN_SIGN}} Sun in the {{SUN_HOUSE}} house — [2–3 paragraphs: sign
    expression + house arena of life + one defining aspect]
  - {{MOON_SIGN}} Moon in the {{MOON_HOUSE}} house — [2–3 paragraphs: emotional
    style, safety needs, comfort patterns, defining aspect]
  - {{ASCENDANT_SIGN}} Rising, ruled by {{CHART_RULER}} — [2–3 paragraphs:
    demeanor, first impressions, approach to new situations; note the chart
    ruler's sign/house because it colors the whole life path]
  - How the three interact: [element/modality harmony or friction between Sun,
    Moon, and Rising — e.g., a Fire Sun with a Water Moon creates a
    "bold outside, tender inside" dynamic]

================================================================================
PART II — BIRTH CHART: PERSONALITY OVERVIEW
================================================================================

2.A  PLANETARY PLACEMENTS AND THEIR MEANINGS
[For EACH planet below, generate a subsection in this fixed format:
   • What the planet governs (its "job" in the psyche)
   • What it means in {{PLANET_SIGN}} (how the job gets done)
   • Which house it occupies (where the job happens) — cross-reference 2.B
   • Its 1–3 strongest aspects (who it "talks to" and how)
   • One practical, client-specific takeaway sentence]

  2.A.1  Sun in {{SUN_SIGN}} — identity, will, purpose
  2.A.2  Moon in {{MOON_SIGN}} — emotions, instincts, security
  2.A.3  Mercury in {{MERCURY_SIGN}} — mind, communication, learning style
  2.A.4  Venus in {{VENUS_SIGN}} — love language, values, aesthetics, money
  2.A.5  Mars in {{MARS_SIGN}} — drive, desire, anger style, how you pursue
  2.A.6  Jupiter in {{JUPITER_SIGN}} — growth, luck, philosophy, expansion
  2.A.7  Saturn in {{SATURN_SIGN}} — structure, discipline, lessons, fears
  2.A.8  Uranus in {{URANUS_SIGN}} — rebellion, innovation, sudden change
  2.A.9  Neptune in {{NEPTUNE_SIGN}} — dreams, spirituality, illusion, art
  2.A.10 Pluto in {{PLUTO_SIGN}} — power, transformation, the underworld
  [Optional premium add-ons:]
  2.A.11 Chiron in {{CHIRON_SIGN}} — the wound that becomes the gift
  2.A.12 North Node in {{NN_SIGN}} / South Node in {{SN_SIGN}} — soul
         direction vs. comfort zone
  2.A.13 Part of Fortune in {{POF_SIGN}} — where joy and luck compound

2.B  THE TWELVE HOUSES: WHERE LIFE HAPPENS
[First, a short primer: signs describe HOW energy behaves; houses describe
WHERE it plays out. Then generate one paragraph for EVERY OCCUPIED house
(houses containing one or more planets, plus the house of the Ascendant and any
house with a significant cusp aspect). Empty houses are not "bad" — include a
brief note on the sign on each empty cusp and its ruling planet's placement, so
no life area is left unaddressed.]

  House 1 — Self, body, first impressions  | planets here: {{H1_PLANETS}}
  House 2 — Money, possessions, self-worth | planets here: {{H2_PLANETS}}
  House 3 — Communication, siblings, early learning | {{H3_PLANETS}}
  House 4 — Home, roots, family, foundation | {{H4_PLANETS}}
  House 5 — Creativity, romance, play, children | {{H5_PLANETS}}
  House 6 — Health, daily routine, work, service | {{H6_PLANETS}}
  House 7 — Partnership, marriage, open enemies | {{H7_PLANETS}}
  House 8 — Intimacy, shared resources, transformation | {{H8_PLANETS}}
  House 9 — Travel, higher learning, belief systems | {{H9_PLANETS}}
  House 10 — Career, reputation, public legacy | {{H10_PLANETS}}
  House 11 — Friends, community, hopes & wishes | {{H11_PLANETS}}
  House 12 — Subconscious, solitude, hidden matters | {{H12_PLANETS}}

  [For each occupied house, cover: (1) the life arena, (2) the sign on the
  cusp and its ruler's placement, (3) each planet inside and what it does to
  that arena, (4) a concrete life example the client will recognize.]

2.C  MAJOR ASPECTS: THE CONVERSATIONS BETWEEN PLANETS
  - Conjunctions, sextiles, squares, trines, oppositions — a one-line primer
    on each aspect type
  - The client's 5–8 strongest exact aspects, each interpreted in plain
    language, e.g., "{{VENUS}} square {{MARS}}: your heart and your desires
    move at different speeds — passion is high but timing feels dramatic."
  - Any stellium ({{STELLIUM_NOTE}}), Grand Trine, T-Square, or Yod patterns,
    with dedicated interpretation.

2.D  SECTION CLOSER — THE FOUR ELEMENTS IN YOUR CHART
[This subsection CONCLUDES the birth chart section. Tally every planet + the
Ascendant (and optionally MC) by element and present the client's actual
distribution: Fire {{FIRE_COUNT}} / Earth {{EARTH_COUNT}} / Air {{AIR_COUNT}} /
Water {{WATER_COUNT}}. Include a simple bar-graph graphic placeholder.]

  FIRE (Aries, Leo, Sagittarius) — inspiration, action, confidence, passion
    • If prominent: visionary energy, natural leadership, enthusiasm that
      rallies others; risk of burnout, impatience, starting more than finishing.
    • If lacking: motivation must be consciously manufactured — client may need
      external deadlines, exercise, or bold company to ignite initiative;
      caution around self-doubt and playing small.
  EARTH (Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn) — practicality, stability, the material world
    • If prominent: reliable, resourceful, excellent follow-through; risk of
      rigidity, over-caution, workaholism, or judging the unproven.
    • If lacking: grounding practices matter — budgeting, routine, and bodily
      care don't come naturally and must be systematized rather than improvised.
  AIR (Gemini, Libra, Aquarius) — intellect, communication, connection, ideas
    • If prominent: quick, curious, socially fluent, idea generators; risk of
      overthinking, detachment, or talking instead of doing.
    • If lacking: client processes through feeling and experience rather than
      discussion — may need to deliberately seek outside perspectives and
      watch for assumptions going unchallenged.
  WATER (Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces) — emotion, intuition, empathy, depth
    • If prominent: emotionally intelligent, intuitive, healing presence; risk
      of absorbing others' feelings, moodiness, or difficulty with boundaries.
    • If lacking: emotions are processed slowly or intellectually — client
      should build rituals (journaling, therapy, honest conversation) that make
      feelings explicit rather than assumed.
  - Synthesis paragraph: name the client's dominant element, their missing or
    weakest element, and 2–3 concrete habits that balance the formula.
  - [Optional: same treatment for the three modalities — Cardinal, Fixed,
    Mutable — as a bonus sidebar.]

================================================================================
PART III — SYNASTRY REPORT: WHAT TO LOOK FOR (PARTNERS & FRIENDS, EQUAL WEIGHT)
================================================================================

[Structural rule: this part gives IDENTICAL depth, page space, and structural
weight to romantic partnership and to friendship. Sections 3.B and 3.C are
mirror images of one another — same number of subsections, same level of
detail. Neither is an afterthought.]

3.A  YOUR RELATIONAL BLUEPRINT (from your natal chart alone)
  3.A.1  What you project onto others: the Descendant ({{DESCENDANT_SIGN}})
         and its ruler — the qualities you're magnetized toward
  3.A.2  How you love: Venus in {{VENUS_SIGN}}/{{VENUS_HOUSE}} house,
         Mars in {{MARS_SIGN}}, Moon in {{MOON_SIGN}} — needs vs. wants
  3.A.3  How you connect and belong: Mercury in {{MERCURY_SIGN}}, the 11th
         house ({{H11_SIGN}} cusp, {{H11_PLANETS}}), and the 3rd house —
         your friendship operating system
  3.A.4  Your non-negotiables: Saturn and Pluto contacts in the natal chart
         that reveal karmic patterns repeated across BOTH romance and friendship

3.B  WHAT TO LOOK FOR IN A ROMANTIC PARTNER  (equal emphasis — full section)
  3.B.1  Elemental & modal complementarity: which partner Sun/Moon/Rising
         elements balance your own (e.g., your {{DOMINANT_ELEMENT}}-heavy
         chart is steadied by an Earth or Water emphasis)
  3.B.2  Key synastry aspects to seek:
         • Sun–Moon conjunctions/trines — core identity and emotional needs
           in the same key
         • Venus–Mars contacts — chemistry and sustained desire
         • Moon–Moon harmony — day-to-day emotional compatibility, home life
         • Mercury contacts — how you'll argue and repair
         • Saturn bonds (conjunct/trine to personal planets) — the glue of
           longevity and commitment
         • Jupiter contacts — mutual growth, generosity, shared adventure
  3.B.3  Aspects to approach with caution: harsh Venus–Saturn or Venus–Pluto
         squares, Mars–Pluto hard aspects, Sun–Sun opposition without
         softeners — not dealbreakers, but pressure points requiring maturity
  3.B.4  Timing note: how your current Venus/Jupiter transits color what you're
         attracting this year (bridge to Part IV)
  3.B.5  A partner-profile paragraph: plain-language description of the person
         your chart is "shopping for" — values, temperament, communication
         style, and the role they play in your growth

3.C  WHAT TO LOOK FOR IN FRIENDS  (equal emphasis — mirror structure of 3.B)
  3.C.1  Elemental & modal complementarity in friendship: which friends balance
         your chart socially (your 11th house sign {{H11_SIGN}} describes the
         friend you need, not just the friend you get)
  3.C.2  Key synastry aspects to seek:
         • Moon–Moon harmony — effortless comfort, emotional safety, the
           "can sit in silence together" test
         • Mercury–Mercury contacts — shared humor, ideas, and conversation
           rhythm; the engine of lasting friendship
         • Venus–Venus contacts — aligned values, tastes, and reciprocity
         • Sun–Sun trines/sextiles — mutual respect for each other's paths
         • 11th-house overlays — their planets in your 11th (and vice versa):
           the classic friendship signature
         • Jupiter bonds — friends who expand your world and champion you
  3.C.3  Aspects to approach with caution: hard Saturn contacts to your Moon
         or Venus (friendships that feel like obligations), Neptune fog
         (friends you idealize then feel betrayed by), Mars squares (competition
         that corrodes warmth) — with advice on boundaries rather than
         blanket avoidance
  3.C.4  Timing note: how current Jupiter/11th-house transits reshape your
         social circle over the next year (bridge to Part IV)
  3.C.5  A friend-profile paragraph: plain-language description of the
         companions your chart thrives with — loyalty style, communication
         cadence, and the role they play in your growth

3.D  RELATIONSHIP READINESS SUMMARY
  - Short synthesis: how 3.B and 3.C together describe a complete relational
    ecosystem — partners and friends meet different needs, and a healthy life
    invests deliberately in both.
  - [Optional paid upgrade: full two-person synastry when the client supplies a
    second birth date/time/location — composite chart, house overlays, and a
    scored compatibility matrix for romance AND friendship dimensions.]

================================================================================
PART IV — TRANSIT REPORT: WEEKLY PREDICTIONS FOR THE NEXT YEAR
================================================================================

[Methodology: overlay the moving sky from {{REPORT_DATE}} through
{{REPORT_DATE_PLUS_1_YEAR}} onto the client's natal chart. Every week is
generated individually — no recycled generic horoscope text. Prioritize
transits by impact: outer planets (Pluto/Neptune/Uranus) to natal personal
points > Saturn & Jupiter transits > Mars transits > lunations. Also track
Mercury/Venus/Mars retrogrades, eclipses, and station days.]

4.A  THE YEAR IN BROAD STROKES (before the weekly detail)
  - Jupiter in {{JUPITER_TRANSIT_SIGN}}: which natal house lights up with
    opportunity — the year's expansion theme
  - Saturn in {{SATURN_TRANSIT_SIGN}}: which natal house demands discipline —
    the year's maturity theme
  - Uranus/Neptune/Pluto degrees contacting natal planets: the once-in-a-
    lifetime undercurrents ({{OUTER_PLANET_NOTES}})
  - Eclipse path: {{ECLIPSE_AXIS}} — the axis of life being reset
  - Retrograde calendar: Mercury ({{MERCURY_RETRO_DATES}}), Venus
    ({{VENUS_RETRO_DATES}}), Mars ({{MARS_RETRO_DATES}})
  - Saturn Return / Jupiter Return / nodal return status, if applicable

4.B  MONTH-BY-MONTH PREAMBLES (12 short paragraphs)
  - For each month: headline theme, the month's dominant transits to the natal
    chart, and the two dates that matter most.

4.C  WEEKLY INCREMENTS — THE NEXT 52 WEEKS
[Generate one entry per week, Week 1 through Week 52. Each entry uses this
exact template. Target 120–200 words per week.]

  ── WEEK {{N}}: {{WEEK_START_DATE}} – {{WEEK_END_DATE}} ─────────────────────
  • Sky this week: [ingresses, stations, lunation phase — e.g., "Full Moon at
    12° {{SIGN}} on {{DATE}}; Mercury stations retrograde {{DATE}}"]
  • Contacting your chart: [named transiting planet → natal planet/house, e.g.,
    "transiting Mars crosses your natal Venus ({{DEGREE}}° {{SIGN}}) Tuesday —
    romance and money both move fast"]
  • Theme: [one-line headline for the week]
  • Love & friendships: [synastry-informed guidance, honoring Part III]
  • Career & money: [guidance tied to natal 2nd/6th/10th houses]
  • Wellbeing & inner life: [guidance tied to Moon and 12th house]
  • Power day: {{BEST_DAY}} — why | Watch-out day: {{CAUTION_DAY}} — why
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  EXAMPLE (illustrative — actual copy generated from the client's chart):
  ── WEEK 1: {{REPORT_DATE}} – {{REPORT_DATE + 6 DAYS}} ──────────────────────
  • Sky this week: New Moon at {{DEGREE}}° {{SIGN}} — a seed-planting lunation
    in your {{HOUSE}} house.
  • Contacting your chart: transiting Jupiter trines your natal Sun
    ({{SUN_DEGREE}}° {{SUN_SIGN}}) midweek — confidence, visibility, and
    generous offers are favored.
  • Theme: Plant one seed you'd be proud to harvest in October.
  • Love & friendships: your {{MOON_SIGN}} Moon wants depth over breadth — one
    honest conversation beats ten pleasant ones.
  • Career & money: pitch, apply, ask — the New Moon in your {{HOUSE}} house
    rewards initiation.
  • Wellbeing & inner life: sleep schedule is the weak point; protect it.
  • Power day: {{DAY}} | Watch-out day: {{DAY}} (Moon squares natal Mars —
    short fuse, choose words slowly).
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  [Repeat through Week 52, ending {{REPORT_DATE_PLUS_1_YEAR}}. Generation
  checklist per week: at least one named transit-to-natal contact; no two
  consecutive weeks with identical theme language; retrograde weeks must
  reference the affected natal house; eclipse weeks receive extended length.]

4.D  HOW TO USE YOUR TRANSIT CALENDAR
  - Transits are weather, not verdicts: they describe conditions; the client's
    free will decides the response.
  - Suggested ritual: read the coming week on Sunday evening; mark power days
    and watch-out days in the client's calendar; revisit the monthly preamble
    on the 1st.

================================================================================
PART V — CLOSING INTEGRATION & DISCLAIMER
================================================================================

5.1  YOUR CHART IN ONE PAGE
  - A condensed recap: top three, dominant element, chart ruler, strongest
    aspect, biggest growth edge (Saturn), greatest gift (Jupiter), what to
    seek in partners, what to seek in friends, and the year's headline transit.

5.2  DISCLAIMER
  - This report is provided for self-reflection, insight, and entertainment
    purposes. Astrology is not a substitute for professional medical, legal,
    financial, or psychological advice. Predictive sections describe symbolic
    weather patterns, not fixed events.

================================================================================
APPENDIX A — GENERATION & QC CHECKLIST (internal, stripped from client copy)
================================================================================
  [ ] Birth time confirmed (or "unknown time" variant used: Rising/houses
      omitted with explanatory note; Moon degree range flagged)
  [ ] Part I leads the report and explains WHY the top three matter before
      interpreting them
  [ ] All 10 core planets covered in 2.A; every occupied house covered in 2.B;
      empty houses addressed via cusp rulers
  [ ] Part II CONCLUDES with the four-element balance (2.D), including explicit

Done — the full template is written to `answer.txt` in the workspace (and committed to git). Here's how it maps to your requirements:

**Part I — The "Top Three" (leads the report)**
Explains *why* Sun, Moon, and Rising matter as a triad (core identity / emotional needs / outer lens — "the cover, the story, and what the story secretly means"), then interprets the client's own three with degrees and houses.

**Part II — Birth Chart: Personality Overview**
- All 10 core planets (plus optional Chiron, Nodes, Part of Fortune) with a fixed format: what the planet governs → what it means in the client's sign → which house → strongest aspects → practical takeaway
- All 12 houses with meanings, including empty houses handled via cusp rulers
- Major aspects section (stelliums, T-squares, etc.)
- **Section closer: Four Elements** — actual Fire/Earth/Air/Water tally from their chart, with explicit "if prominent" and "if lacking" readings for each element, plus balancing habits

**Part III — Synastry: Partners & Friends at Equal Weight**
Sections 3.B (romantic partner) and 3.C (friends) are deliberate mirror images — same five subsections each (complementarity, aspects to seek, caution aspects, timing note, profile paragraph). The QC checklist even enforces ±10% word-count parity so friendship never gets shortchanged.

**Part IV — Transit Report: Weekly for the Next Year**
- "Year in broad strokes" first (Jupiter/Saturn house themes, eclipses, retrograde calendar, Saturn Return check)
- 12 monthly preambles
- Exactly 52 weekly entries with a locked template: sky events → transit-to-natal contacts → theme → love/friendships → career/money → wellbeing → power day & watch-out day, with a filled example week

**Part V + Appendix** — one-page recap, entertainment/self-reflection disclaimer, and an internal QC checklist (birth-time-unknown variant, no unresolved placeholders, no duplicate copy across clients).

Every field uses `{{TOKENS}}` so it plugs directly into an automated generation pipeline. One business suggestion: make exact birth time a hard requirement at intake — without it the Rising sign and houses (a third of the report) can't be computed, and the template includes a fallback variant for that case.
